statement: For every complete finite simple SRG(99,14,1,2), count actual induced rook-nine vertex subsets once and define d_T=6-r_T for each actual triangle. If R=227 and no triangle has deficiency three, it is impossible that exactly eight triangles have deficiency two. Equivalently, the positive deficiency family cannot consist of exactly eight deficiency-one and eight deficiency-two triangles, with every other triangle of deficiency zero. This does not exclude R227 or an arbitrary even eight-triangle incidence relation.
assumptions: R=227 counts actual induced9-vertex rook subsets once by their vertex sets
no actual triangle has deficiency d_T=6-r_T equal to three

A root Moore bound forces a C4; its complement four-node induced subgraph is C4 with bijective attachments.
The two C4 edge sets under attachment share a perfectmatching or coincide, so every cross edge and every dual edge lies in C4.
An actual pair of intersecting or disjoint triangles fixes any containing rook; two distinct rooks share at mostone actual triangle.
Even symmetric difference with a rook at overlap>=4 would give impossible even2/4 or an induced even6 rook sharing2 triangles.
Every dual C4 becomes an uncovered actualsquare, hence every odd intersection fills both D1 defect slots.
A D2 at odd support needs other D2 nodes and fan weight21>P16, so all D2 are outside.
Eight D2 outside have three localK3 points each; globaldegree6 gives K8-minusmatching.
Four common F2 neighbors would all meet an adjacent pair's point, where only one positive thirdnode exists.
